message.reasoning:
We need to extract triplets from the description of the flag. Identify entities: "Flag of the United States" (subject). Relations: "instance of" maybe? But we need explicit facts.

Text: "Flag of the United States

United States of America Names The American flag, The Stars and Stripes; Red, White, and Blue; Old Glory; The Star - Spangled Banner; US flag; United States flag Use National flag and ensign Proportion 10: 19 Adopted June 14, 1777 (original 13 - star version) July 4, 1960 (current 50 - star version) Design Thirteen horizontal stripes alternating red and white; in the canton, 50 white stars of alternating numbers of six and five per horizontal row on a blue field"

We need to parse.

Subject likely "Flag of the United States". Could also treat "United States flag" as same.

Relations:

- "country" or "used by": The flag is the national flag and ensign of United States of America. So relation: "country" maybe "United States of America". Use "used by" maybe "used by" relation. We'll choose "country" or "used by". In Wikidata, property P17 is "country". For a flag, property "country" is used. So (Flag of the United States, country, United States of America).

- "name": multiple alternative names. Each name is a separate triplet: (Flag of the United States, name, The American flag) etc. Need subject_type flag (object_type maybe "name").

- "use": "National flag and ensign". Could be relation "use" with object "national flag" and "ensign". But maybe "use" relation: (Flag of the United States, use, national flag) and (Flag of the United States, use, ensign). But "national flag" is a type, not an entity. Might be okay.

- "proportion": 10:19. So relation "proportion" with object "10:19". object_type "ratio". Provide qualifier maybe none.

- "adopted": two dates: original version June 14, 1777 (original 13-star version) and current version July 4, 1960 (current 50-star version). So we need two triplets: (Flag of the United States, date of adoption, June 14, 1777) with qualifier maybe "original version" or "star count" 13-star. Could add qualifier "star count" 13. Also (Flag of the United States, date of adoption, July 4, 1960) with qualifier "star count" 50.

We need relation "date of adoption". object_type date.

- "design": description. Could be relation "design description". Might be "design". object is the description string. Could be split: "thirteen horizontal stripes alternating red and white" and "canton contains 50 white stars of alternating numbers of six and five per horizontal row on a blue field". Could be separate triplets: (Flag of the United States, design element, thirteen horizontal stripes alternating red and white). (Flag of the United States, design element, 50 white stars of alternating numbers of six and five per horizontal row on a blue field). object_type "description".

- Also "color": red, white, blue. Could be relation "color". But not explicit as separate; part of design. Could add (Flag of the United States, color, red), (Flag of the United States, color, white), (Flag of the United States, color, blue). Might be okay.

- "star count": 13 original, 50 current. Could be relation "number of stars". Provide qualifiers for version. But we have adoption dates with qualifiers.

We need to include qualifiers correctly: For adoption date, qualifier "star count" maybe "13-star version". Use qualifier relation "star count" object "13". Similarly for 50.

Also qualifier "version" maybe "original". But we can include "version" qualifier.

Now produce JSON.

Define subject_type "flag". object_type accordingly: for country "country", for name "name", for use "use type"? maybe "category". For proportion "ratio". For date "date". For design element "description". For color "color". For star count "integer".

subject: "Flag of the United States"

qualifiers: []

Triplet 2-? names list: names: "The American flag", "The Stars and Stripes", "Red, White, and Blue", "Old Glory", "The Star-Spangled Banner", "US flag", "United States flag". Each separate.

Triplet for each name: relation "name". object each name. qualifiers none.

Triplet for use: maybe two: "national flag" and "ensign". relation "use". object "national flag". qualifiers none. Another for "ensign".

Triplet for proportion: relation "proportion". object "10:19". qualifiers none.

Triplet for adoption date 1: relation "date of adoption". object "June 14, 1777". qualifiers: [{"relation":"star count","object":"13"} , {"relation":"version","object":"original"}]. Might also include "point in time" but date is object.

Triplet for adoption date 2: relation "date of adoption". object "July 4, 1960". qualifiers: [{"relation":"star count","object":"50"},{"relation":"version","object":"current"}].

Triplet for design element stripes: relation "design element". object "thirteen horizontal stripes alternating red and white". qualifiers none.

Triplet for design element stars: relation "design element". object "50 white stars of alternating numbers of six and five per horizontal row on a blue field". qualifiers none.

Triplet for colors: maybe separate: relation "color". object "red". etc.

Now produce JSON.

Check qualifiers format: list of dicts with relation and object strings.

subject_type "flag". object_type for name "name". For use maybe "category". For proportion "ratio". For date "date". For design element "description". For color "color". For star count qualifier object type integer but qualifiers don't have types.
